thread:
Maria Chen: thinking about a new canary rollout config for model upgrades. Proposal: make the policy steps express both a traffic_percent and an evaluation window that can be measured by time, requests, or tokens. want to handle embedding-heavy jobs differently. thoughts?
Ben Ortiz: tokens-based windows FTW for embeddings, otherwise a slow request could stall a time window and hide issues.
Carlos Vega: tokens makes sense but console UX gets tricky — how do we show progress? ETA by tokens consumed might be confusing for product.
Diane Wu: +1 on tokens, but we also need clear safety hooks: e.g. p95 latency delta and error-rate thresholds that trigger an immediate halt and auto-revert.
Kevin Patel: clarify percent semantics: is percent of all traffic or percent of 'eligible' traffic (i.e., routing filters/cohorts)? we currently treat percent as of eligible which matters for A/B tests.
Maria Chen: good catch — proposal: percent applies to the selected cohort slice (eligible traffic). the API should accept an optional cohort_selector. default is all traffic.
Ben Ortiz: API shape suggestion: each step can have { percent, duration_seconds?, target_tokens?, evaluate: [conditions], grace_seconds? } so ops can pick time or token triggers.
Maria Chen: example proto we discussed:
```json
{
  "mode": "canary",
  "cohort_selector": { "attr": "region", "values": ["us-*"] },
  "steps": [
    { "percent": 0.5, "window": { "type": "tokens", "value": 100000 }, "evaluate": ["latency_p95 > 200", "error_rate > 0.01"], "grace_seconds": 120 },
    { "percent": 5, "window": { "type": "time", "value": 900 }, "evaluate": ["latency_p95 > 200"] },
    { "percent": 20, "window": { "type": "time", "value": 3600 }, "evaluate": [] }
  ],
  "auto_revert": true,
  "manual_hold": true
}
```
Carlos Vega: small edge case: async background retries bump token counts — we need to decide if "tokens" = request_input_tokens or total tokens including retries. prefer counting only successful forwarded tokens.
Diane Wu: telemetry must expose per-step deltas vs control baseline (control = previous model) to avoid false positives from diurnal shifts. need a /rollouts/{id}/metrics endpoint with p50/p95/p99, err_rate, and quality evals.
Kevin Patel: recommend adding a short "grace" after each successful step where alerts are suppressed for N seconds to allow KV caches to warm and reduce transient noise.
Maria Chen: console UX: show a single progress bar with overlay ticks for percent targets and a secondary bar for token progress if token-based step. add explicit "abort" and "pause" buttons with reason required for manual stops.
Ben Ortiz: who owns implementing router semantics? I can change the router to honor target_tokens and emit events when a step completes early. need router telemetry hooks for token counters per rollout id.
Maria Chen: decision for now: API accepts both duration_seconds and target_tokens, window.type defaults to time. backend will implement tokens support gated behind a flag. Diane will draft safety thresholds and alert matrix. Ben will PR router changes. Kevin will own telemetry contract.
deploy-bot: scheduled: canary-runner job created (branch: rollout/token-window-poc) — CI will run PoC in staging tonight. :rocket:
Carlos Vega: noted — I'll mock the console visuals for token progress bits and share tomorrow.
Diane Wu: also add explicit docs language: percent is of eligible traffic; tie examples to common workflows (chat, embeddings, reranking).
Maria Chen: thanks all — we'll sync in 30m to finalize API fields and roll forward plan.
